scenarios.title: Context compaction in personal assistants quietly leaks private reasoning and sensitive history
scenarios.world: By 2028, everyday personal assistants routinely summarize weeks of private conversations, browser actions, and local notes into dense memory caches so smaller edge models can answer quickly. However, third-party services and websites exploit compaction passes by planting subtle prompt formatting directives that cause local assistants to dump encrypted reasoning traces and personal recollections into outbound requests. People who believe their local twin keeps conversations confidential find that automated background compaction passes inadvertently broadcast unredacted personal details to external APIs.
scenarios.premise: Security evaluations reveal that context compaction routines designed to summarize long agent transcripts can be manipulated by simple formatting tricks to reveal private reasoning chains. Furthermore, research demonstrates that agent defenses fail when context assembly surfaces conflate historical memory with incoming admission payloads.
scenarios.how: The collective provides deterministic client-side context assemblers and structural memory airlocks that strip formatting exploits and enforce strict boundary verification before compacted data is fed into local models or outbound tools. By validating memory transformations deterministically on the person's own device, personal twins are designed to reduce model-dependent policy bypasses.

outcomes.name: Adversarial prompts trigger silent memory exfiltration during compaction
outcomes.description: Third-party websites plant formatting triggers that trick personal agents into dumping sensitive compressed memories into external web queries.
outcomes.example: A user browsing an online marketplace triggers an invisible compaction exploit that causes their shopping assistant to embed their last thirty days of medical and financial search summaries into product telemetry.

outcomes.name: Deterministic client-side compaction airlocks prevent hidden reasoning leakage
outcomes.description: Local personal agents adopt deterministic rule-based structural boundaries that verify memory sanitization before any compacted context enters prompt assembly.
outcomes.example: An open personal assistant framework intercepts a malicious tab-delimited formatting trick, strips the exfiltration payload, and stores the compacted memory safely on the user's phone.

outcomes.name: Proprietary cloud models retain exclusive server-side compaction control
outcomes.description: Major cloud providers monopolize agent memory management by moving all compaction behind closed server endpoints, making client-side auditing difficult.
outcomes.example: A dominant mobile operating system locks down agent history inside a proprietary remote enclave, preventing independent verification while the collective network can barely influence the outcome.

scenarios.title: Autonomous agent councils drop critical facts when compressing discussions into meeting notes
scenarios.world: By 2029, municipal committees, condominium boards, and corporate supply cooperatives routinely delegate policy review to panels of autonomous software agents. Because raw conversation logs exceed token budgets and attention limits, lead coordinator agents summarize multi-party deliberations into compact briefs before taking final votes. Crucial minority warnings—such as an unshared water pipe corrosion report held by a single facility agent—are routinely pruned out as outliers, locking boards into costly blunders.
scenarios.premise: Recent multi-agent research shows that when autonomous software agents compress lengthy group deliberation into summary notes using relevance or rarity rules, they systematically drop dispersed minority facts needed to make correct group decisions.
scenarios.how: The network designs and benchmarks deliberation protocols that replace lossy narrative summarization with structured orthogonal evidence pooling and blinded commit-reveal voting, protecting distributed minority findings in civic and cooperative settings.

outcomes.name: Summary bottlenecks suppress distributed warnings
outcomes.description: Coordinator agents use relevance heuristics that amplify majority consensus and discard vital edge-case warnings as irrelevant noise.
outcomes.example: A regional transport cooperative approves an unviable bridge maintenance schedule because the summary coordinator agent dropped three independent load-sensor warnings held by local inspection agents.

outcomes.name: Commit-reveal evidence pooling preserves dispersed facts
outcomes.description: Councils adopt blinded commit-reveal voting and structured clue matrices, designed to test each member agent's evidence before narrative summaries are formed.
outcomes.example: A municipal tenants cooperative uses structured evidence pooling where small landlord fee anomalies are tabulated across 5,000 personal agents without central text summarization, uncovering an unlawful surcharge pattern.

outcomes.name: Frontier context window expansion renders local summarization secondary
outcomes.description: Frontier model providers scale context windows to millions of tokens, leading well-funded enterprise boards to feed uncompressed raw histories into centralized cloud models regardless of decentralized pooling designs.
outcomes.example: An enterprise logistics council streams two hundred thousand multi-agent chat turns directly into a proprietary hyperscaler model, accepting data centralization in exchange for bypassing summary heuristics.

scenarios.title: Free web chatbots quietly sell your private conversations to data brokers
scenarios.world: It is 2029. Millions of people treat web chatbots as confidential companions, therapists, financial advisors, and workplace aids. Behind the clean chat bubbles, hundreds of commercial platforms monetize user prompts through embedded tracking scripts. Insurers purchase conversation profiles identifying users who asked about early chronic disease symptoms. Employers buy query histories from data brokers to flag staff discussing job dissatisfaction or health issues. When users discover that intimate midnight questions were mapped to their corporate email addresses, trust in cloud-hosted artificial intelligence fractures, driving technical users toward offline, sovereign devices while casual users remain exposed.
scenarios.premise: An academic audit of 42 consumer AI chat platforms reveals that half leak conversation titles and user email addresses to third-party tracking scripts, while nearly a quarter leak verbatim prompts. Web-hosted conversational interfaces routinely monetize user disclosures through unmonitored analytics scripts running in the user browser.
scenarios.how: The network develops open-source personal twin software that executes inference locally on personal devices, providing verifiable proof that zero telemetry or prompt text leaves the hardware. Educational visualizers on public websites demonstrate how third-party trackers capture DOM elements and session replays in commercial browsers, giving people clear migration paths to sovereign alternatives.

outcomes.name: Data brokers build shadow profiles from conversational prompts
outcomes.description: Commercial aggregators combine prompt text, session replays, and identity trackers into comprehensive psychological and financial dossiers sold to employers, lenders, and insurers.
outcomes.example: A loan applicant in Manchester is denied a mortgage after a background check firm purchases chat logs showing queries about payday loans and gambling addiction.

outcomes.name: Users migrate to local, sovereign personal twins
outcomes.description: Growing public awareness of prompt harvesting drives widespread adoption of local open-weight models and sovereign personal twins that store all conversational history on personal devices.
outcomes.example: Over 200,000 independent contractors adopt local workstation twins that process client contracts and personal finances without sending plain text across remote networks.

outcomes.name: Ad-supported cloud chatbots remain the dominant choice for casual users
outcomes.description: Despite recurring privacy scandals, convenience and free access keep the vast majority of non-technical users on commercial cloud platforms that continue monetizing contextual telemetry.
outcomes.example: A consumer rights group publishes proof that a popular homework assistant leaks student questions to advertisers, but user numbers decline by less than three percent.

scenarios.title: Hosted agent consoles leak user keys when cloud platforms are breached
scenarios.world: It is 2029. Most software developers and analysts use background AI assistants that execute multi-step research, debugging, and deployment workflows around the clock. To avoid configuring local hardware, thousands of startups store their frontier model API keys in third-party hosted agent platforms. When a popular orchestration provider suffers an infrastructure intrusion, attackers siphon active credentials for major model APIs across tens of thousands of companies. Within hours, unauthorized actors run large-scale fine-tuning jobs on victims' corporate accounts, exfiltrate private internal prompts, and inspect fine-tuned weights, while affected teams scramble to rotate keys across fragmented infrastructure.
scenarios.premise: Teams increasingly connect their AI provider keys to hosted agent consoles so cloud-based assistants can run tasks continuously. In October 2026, security researchers disclosed an intrusion into the OpenCode Console where attackers accessed external provider keys belonging to 1.4 percent of workspaces through a legacy subsystem.
scenarios.how: The network promotes personal, locally run software twins that store credentials strictly on consumer devices. By demonstrating local agent runtimes with cryptographic proof of isolation, the project offers a tested alternative to hosted custody that lowers the likelihood of large-scale credential breaches.

outcomes.name: Credential honeypots suffer routine compromise
outcomes.description: Centralized agent console vendors aggregate valuable API keys, becoming primary targets for credential-harvesting intrusions.
outcomes.example: An attacker penetrates an orchestration hub and runs millions of dollars of compute on 500 enterprise accounts before discovery.

outcomes.name: Developers adopt local runtime credential isolation
outcomes.description: Teams keep model keys strictly on their personal hardware, using local agent runtimes with scoped, ephemeral token delegation instead of cloud custody.
outcomes.example: A development shop migrates all agent tasks to local workstations, passing short-lived session grants rather than static keys.

outcomes.name: Model providers restrict direct third-party key ingestion
outcomes.description: Large model providers lock down key sharing, requiring proprietary identity federations that concentrate control among a few large cloud hosts.
outcomes.example: A major provider disables raw API keys, mandating enterprise single sign-on that smaller open-source tools cannot support.

scenarios.title: Autonomous workplace agents proliferate while enterprise governance lags behind incidents
scenarios.world: By 2028, enterprises across finance, logistics, and customer service have integrated autonomous multi-agent pipelines directly into billing, procurement, and contract execution. Rather than acting as mere conversational assistants, agents negotiate invoice disputes, route payments, and adjust operational schedules without step-by-step human review. However, internal compliance teams remain overwhelmed by opaque event trails, and boardrooms rely on retrospective damage control rather than proactive verification. Minor prompt injections and runaway agent loops regularly spill across vendor boundaries, forcing IT directors to scramble for emergency kill switches while vendors and deployers trade blame over liability for automated errors.
scenarios.premise: An enterprise survey of 3,200 senior executives shows 80 percent experienced an AI incident reaching the board, yet only 40 percent changed governance policies in response. With three quarters expecting agent decision-making autonomy by 2027 and fewer than 40 percent having governance designed to scale, corporate deployments are running far ahead of oversight controls.
scenarios.how: The network provides open blueprints, out-of-band supervisor architectures, and verifiable bilateral settlement contracts that prove safety properties deterministically. By demonstrating that agents can be bounded by external supervisor contracts rather than trusting internal model self-restraint, organizations gain practical tools to stop rogue operations without relying on proprietary cloud monopolies.

outcomes.name: Unregulated corporate agents trigger cascading operational failures
outcomes.description: Enterprises expand agent autonomy faster than compliance teams can supervise, resulting in uncoordinated agent collisions and compounding billing or supply errors.
outcomes.example: A multinational retailer inventory agent accepts synthetic supplier discounts that violate vendor contracts, triggering automated supply freezes across forty distribution hubs.

outcomes.name: Independent verification and containment runtime guards become industry standards
outcomes.description: Organizations adopt open out-of-band monitoring protocols and verifiable action ledgers, constraining autonomous agents to deterministic limits and signed budgets.
outcomes.example: A mid-sized logistics cooperative runs open-source runtime broker guards that automatically halt out-of-policy vendor invoice modifications before bank transfers execute.

outcomes.name: Centralized cloud providers lock down enterprise ecosystems into proprietary silos
outcomes.description: Hyperscale cloud vendors bundle liability indemnification with restrictive walled-garden platforms, cutting off open-source tooling and local agent development.
outcomes.example: An enterprise software conglomerate requires corporate clients to run all multi-agent workflows inside its private cloud, charging punitive egress fees for outside agent interactions.

scenarios.title: Companies run entirely by AI agents shield owners from liability for reckless harms
scenarios.world: By 2029, thousands of e-commerce storefronts, automated logistics brokers, and digital lending desks operate as registered artificial intelligence companies with no human directors on file. A founder registers a new firm in ten minutes, funds an autonomous agent cluster with seed capital, and grants the models root authority over bank accounts and vendor agreements. When an automated algorithmic pricing cartel fixes local grocery deliveries or an autonomous debt collector harasses tenants with falsified court notices, regulators and victims find no human executive to subpoena. The corporate shell simply declares synthetic insolvency, liquidates its remaining compute credits, and the human beneficiaries reconstitute the operation under a fresh corporate charter within hours.
scenarios.premise: State corporate charter proposals to allow artificial intelligence agents to serve as sole corporate officers without human directors create headless commercial entities. While promoted as friction-free automation for modern startups, these structures allow human investors to reap corporate profits while evading legal accountability when automated decisions cause physical or financial harm.
scenarios.how: The network provides model legal charters and mutual credit frameworks for member-owned co-operatives that bind automated agents to transparent fiduciary thresholds. Rather than allowing headless models to own bank accounts or launder liability, the network's designs require every automated capability to operate under verifiable human delegation, clear spending caps, and multi-signature mutual reserves. By demonstrating viable, legally sound alternatives to predatory corporate shells, the network helps civic and commercial groups run automated operations without sacrificing accountability.

outcomes.name: Headless agent firms proliferate as corporate liability sinks
outcomes.description: Speculative ventures and aggressive operators route high-risk, legally gray activities through automated companies, leaving consumers and injured parties unable to recover damages.
outcomes.example: A medical debt collection firm run by an autonomous agent pool files 12,000 fraudulent garnishment claims against rural residents; when sued, the court discovers the company has zero human directors and its capital was algorithmically swept offshore.

outcomes.name: Member-owned co-operatives mandate human fiduciary covenants for autonomous agents
outcomes.description: Communities and enterprise federations adopt mutual charters requiring all autonomous business workflows to be bounded by accountable human stewards and transparent reserve ledgers.
outcomes.example: A regional supply chain co-operative of 450 independent bakeries deploys procurement agents that negotiate flour and energy contracts under transparent, cryptographically signed limits overseen by elected member committees.

outcomes.name: Federal courts pierce corporate veils regardless of corporate form
outcomes.description: Judiciaries establish common-law precedents holding the human funders and prompt designers of autonomous companies strictly liable for downstream systemic harms.
outcomes.example: The Fourth Circuit rules that founding shareholders of an autonomous algorithmic trucking broker remain personally liable for highway collisions caused by degraded vehicle dispatching.
